Yeah, it's an oversimplification, but getting something both stable and thinner than an individual atom is unachieved, as far as I know. And your "measurable size" can be tricky to define. Consider a hydrogen atom, with it's single proton nucleus and electron running around the outside. The area that usually contains the electron is called the "electron cloud." It's hard to define the edge of the cloud because the electron has some non-zero chance of being found any distance from its nucleus. So we made up a cut-off and said that the closest volume to the nucleus where the electron spends 90% of it's time is the cloud. Really this cloud gets keeps getting thinner as you move away from the nucleus and never quite goes away.
